extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners, patent owners, and USPTO stakeholders (PTAB counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for PTAB AIA trial practice, including precedential-panel criteria, motions to amend (MTA) practice, joinder/time-bar considerations, reissue/reexamination interactions, evidentiary rules for oral hearings and rehearing, and technical/hearing procedures. Targets practice and decisionmaking at the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential Opinion Panel (POP) designation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for referring decisions to the Precedential Opinion Panel (POP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As outlined in PTAB SOP2: constitutional questions; important questions regarding statutes, rules, regulations; important issues regarding precedential case law; issues of broad applicability to the Board; resolve conflicts between Board decisions; promote certainty and consistency. Default POP composition: Director; Commissioner for Patents; PTAB Chief Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP discretionary joinder under 35 U.S.C. § 315(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for whether the Board will allow a petitioner to be joined to a proceeding in which it is already a party and whether new issues may be joined into an existing proceeding under § 315(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 315(c) provides discretion to allow same-party joinder and joinder of new issues; the existence of a time bar under § 315(b) is one factor among several. The Board will exercise discretion only in limited circumstances—where fairness requires it and to avoid undue prejudice. Exemplary factors to consider: actions taken by patent owner in co-pending litigation (e.g., late addition of newly asserted claims); conduct of the parties; the stage and schedule of an existing inter partes review; non-exclusive factors from General Plastic Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Canon Kabushiki Kaisha (factors supporting exercise of discretion to deny institution under § 314(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for proving a reference is a 'printed publication' at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard for what a petitioner must establish to qualify an asserted reference as a printed publication at the institution stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The POP in Hulu v. Sound View ordered review on 'What is required for a petitioner to establish that an asserted reference qualifies as “printed publication” at the institution stage?' The POP accepted additional briefing and responses; the question is under review (no detailed test provided on these slides), indicating that the sufficiency of evidence at institution is a scrutinized issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for amending RPI identification post-institution while maintaining petition date
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors the Board considers when a petitioner seeks to amend Real Party-in-Interest (RPI) identification after institution but seeks to keep the petition's original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include attempts to circumvent the § 315(b) bar; bad faith by petitioner; prejudice to patent owner caused by delay; gamesmanship by petitioner. Boards have both denied and granted such amendments depending on these factors (see Proppant Express, Ventex, Adello Biologics decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend (MTA) requirements and guidance (Lectrosonics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive and procedural requirements the Board expects when a patent owner files a motion to amend during an AIA trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes: allowance for contingent motions to amend; the burden of persuasion the Office applies when considering patentability of substitute claims; requirement that a patent owner propose a reasonable number of substitute claims; requirement that the amendment respond to a ground of unpatentability involved in the trial; attention to the scope of the proposed substitute claims; requirement that a patent owner provide a claim listing with its motion to amend; default page limits that apply to motion to amend briefing; and the duty of candor. (This guidance reflects statutory/regulatory requirements as interpreted in Lectrosonics v. Zaxcom.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds considered for substitute claims (§311(b) v. §316(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on petitioners and the Board with respect to grounds of unpatentability for existing claims and for substitute claims proposed in an MTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 311(b) limits a petitioner to requesting cancellation of existing claims only under §§ 102 and 103. However, § 316(d) does not prevent the Board from considering other grounds of unpatentability (e.g., § 101) with respect to substitute claims not yet part of the patent; petitioners may raise, and the Board may consider, such other grounds for substitute claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new evidence or new arguments at oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule that evidence or arguments not previously submitted in the proceeding generally may not be presented at oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Trial Practice Guide and DePuy Synthes v. MEDIDEA: a party may rely upon evidence previously submitted in the proceeding and only present arguments relied upon in the papers previously submitted. New evidence submitted at oral hearing is considered new and is generally not permitted (e.g., inventor testimony at hearing is new evidence if no prior declaration was submitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for permitting live testimony at oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances under which the Board will order or permit live testimony during oral hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live testimony is expected to be ordered only in limited circumstances, such as where witness demeanor is critical to assessing credibility. Factors to consider: the importance of the witness’s testimony to the case (whether case-dispositive), and whether the witness is a fact witness. The Board does not expect live testimony in most oral arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause standard for admitting new evidence with a rehearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: When evidence not already of record may be admitted in connection with a request for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence not of record at the time of the decision will not be admitted absent a showing of good cause (Huawei Device Co. v. Optis Wireless Tech.). A party should request a conference call prior to filing a rehearing request to argue good cause, or alternatively argue in the rehearing request why good cause exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of institution for inefficient use of resources (§314(a) / SAS considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board may deny institution of a petition because proceeding would be an inefficient use of Board resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel may evaluate challenges and determine whether, in the interests of efficient administration of the Office and the integrity of the patent system (see 35 U.S.C. § 316(b)), the entire petition should be denied under § 314(a) when petitioner demonstrates a reasonable likelihood of prevailing only for a limited subset of claims or grounds. Examples: institution denied where only two dependent claims out of 20 had a reasonable likelihood of prevailing; institution on all claims/grounds based on arguments directed to only two claims/one ground is inefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA pilot program options for patent owners
rubrics_metrics.description: New pilot procedural options (effective March 15, 2019) available to patent owners regarding motions to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two new options: (1) Patent owner may choose to receive Preliminary Guidance (PG) from the Board on its MTA; (2) Patent owner may choose to file a revised MTA after receiving petitioner’s opposition and/or the Board’s PG (if requested). If PO does not elect either option, AIA trial practice remains essentially unchanged (with minor timing extensions for some later-filed papers). MTA and revised MTA are contingent unless PO indicates otherwise (e.g., by canceling original claims). If PO files a revised MTA, Board issues a revised scheduling order, there is one additional paper per party, and new briefing and oral hearing schedules. Final written decision addresses only substitute claims at issue in the latest filed MTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA pilot program implementation and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing, retroactivity, and reassessment policy for the MTA pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot effective date is publication date of notice (March 15, 2019) and applies to all AIA trials instituted on or after that date. USPTO anticipates reassessing the pilot approximately one year from the effective date and may terminate or continue the program (with or without modifications) based on stakeholder feedback and program effectiveness. Topics addressed in notice include timelines, retroactivity of applying pilot, Board preliminary decision, opportunity to file revised MTA, contingent MTAs, and opting-out of pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for amendments through reissue or reexamination during AIA trials
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Office will consider reissue applications or requests for reexamination in relation to AIA trial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will consider a reissue application or request for reexamination any time before, but not after, either (1) Office issues a certificate that cancels all claims of a patent, or (2) Federal Circuit issues a mandate in relation to a decision that finds all claims invalid/unpatentable. The Office will not issue a trial certificate canceling all claims until after the appeal filing deadline has passed (63 days after FWD or rehearing decision) or all appellate matters are finally resolved. Patent owners may file reissue or reexamination before, during, or after an AIA trial concludes with a Final Written Decision, provided timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for stays of parallel reissue or reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board will stay or suspend parallel Office proceedings that involve a patent at issue in an AIA proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board ordinarily will stay a parallel Office proceeding where good cause exists—for example, when an ongoing AIA proceeding addresses the same or overlapping claims. The Board typically considers motions to stay (or may impose a stay sua sponte) after institution of an AIA trial and before the filing of a notice of appeal or the deadline for filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit. Notices describe non-limiting factors the Board and Patents units consider when deciding whether to grant or lift stays or suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to lift a stay after a Final Written Decision (FWD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards the Board applies when a patent owner moves to lift a stay of a parallel proceeding after a Final Written Decision issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO files a motion to lift a stay after a FWD, the Board typically will lift the stay absent reasons not to do so. The Board typically will lift a stay if PO proposes amendments in a reissue or reexamination in a meaningful way not previously considered by the Office. Meaningful amendments include narrowing the scope of claims considered in the AIA proceeding or otherwise attempting to resolve issues identified in the FWD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of reissue applications during Federal Circuit appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: How reissue applications are handled when a Federal Circuit appeal is ongoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Federal Circuit appeal remains ongoing when an examiner identifies allowable subject matter in a reissue application, the Office typically will not pass the reissue to allowance until the Federal Circuit appeal concludes. The examiner may need to reevaluate allowable subject matter in view of the Federal Circuit decision. After appeal concludes, PO may proceed to issuance, file an RCE, or abandon the reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination procedures and interaction with appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: How ex parte reexamination proceedings proceed and interact with Federal Circuit appeals on the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike reissue, POs cannot abandon ex parte reexamination once started; reexaminations proceed with special dispatch to completion (35 U.S.C. § 305). After the Office lifts a stay (or determines a stay is not appropriate), reexamination typically will continue to completion notwithstanding a Federal Circuit appeal of a FWD on the same patent. If the Office identifies allowable subject matter or determines claims unpatentable, it typically will issue a NIRC and reexamination certificate even if a related Federal Circuit appeal is ongoing—unless PO timely files a notice of appeal in the reexamination. To prevent a reexamination certificate from canceling original patent claims that are separately on appeal at the Federal Circuit, PO must timely file an appeal of any final rejection in reexamination to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/connectivity features and public access for PTAB hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical capabilities and options for participating in PTAB hearings and for public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All hearing rooms are equipped with Video Teleconferencing Equipment (VTC) and can connect to each other. Judges not located in regional offices connect via Cisco Jabber. Attorneys may connect by their own VTC equipment, by going to a regional office, via WebEx, or telephonically (audio only). Hearing connections are monitored by the VTC Operations team and a hearings team member. Panels can participate from home during inclement weather or office closures. PTAB will consider parties’ preference of hearing location and increase public access to view hearings from any Regional Office; audio-visual systems are being updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision scope after revised MTA filing
rubrics_metrics.description: What the Final Written Decision (FWD) will address when a revised motion to amend has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a patent owner files a revised MTA, the Final Written Decision addresses only the substitute claims at issue in the latest filed MTA (i.e., the most recent set of proposed substitute claims).
